::: family-head
<p class="tagline"><span class="num">01</span>Plant trait data</p>

<h2>AusTraits family</h2>

AusTraits is an open, curated database of traits for the Australian flora, harmonised from hundreds of sources. Around it sit the tools that build it, define its traits, resolve its plant names and serve its data.

::: family-links
[austraits.org →](https://austraits.org) [Paper →](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-021-01006-6)
:::
:::

::: {#austraits-tools}
:::
::::
:::::

::::: {#plant .family .family-plant}
:::: wrap
::: family-head
<p class="tagline"><span class="num">02</span>Vegetation models</p>

<h2>plant family</h2>

The plant model simulates how traits shape the growth, competition and evolution of plants in forests. The family around it adds documentation, community assembly, site and species set-up, leaf physiology, fire and visualisation.

::: family-links
[Overstorey guide →](https://traitecoevo.github.io/overstorey/) [Paper →](https://doi.org/10.1111/2041-210X.12525)
:::
:::

::: {#plant-tools}
:::
::::
:::::

::::: {#havplot .family .family-havplot}
:::: wrap
::: family-head
<p class="tagline"><span class="num">03</span>Vegetation plot data</p>

<h2>HAVPlot family</h2>

HAVPlot, the Harmonised Australian Vegetation Plot dataset, brings vegetation plot surveys from across Australia into one compilation of more than 200,000 plots. We are rebuilding it as an open, documented workflow that does for plot data what AusTraits does for trait data. The repositories will open as the work matures.

::: family-links
[Paper →](https://doi.org/10.1111/ecog.06426)
:::
:::

::: {#havplot-tools}

<h2>About</h2>

traitecoevo is the shared GitHub home of the Cornsters (**Corn**well + Fal**ster**): the labs of Daniel Falster and Will Cornwell at UNSW Sydney, with our students, postdocs and collaborators. The tools here grew out of our research, and many are now used well beyond it.

Current and past lab members are listed on our lab websites:

[Falster lab →](https://danielfalster.com/members){.btn-outline} [Cornwell lab →](https://willcornwell.org/){.btn-outline}
:::

::: install
<h3>Install our R packages</h3>

Most of our R packages are built on [R-universe](https://traitecoevo.r-universe.dev), so you can install them without extra tools:

```r
install.packages(
  "austraits",
  repos = c("https://traitecoevo.r-universe.dev",
            "https://cloud.r-project.org")
)
```
:::
